front: Three parts of a good ratio comment
back: Direction and size (with figures), a likely cause, and the effect or advice.

front: What changes the gross profit margin?
back: Selling prices, buying prices, sales mix, theft or damage of inventory, and errors in inventory valuation.

front: What changes profit for the year but not gross profit?
back: Expenses (wages, rent, depreciation, irrecoverable debts, interest) and other income (rent received, commission, discount received).
Capital expenditure, depreciation, drawings, changes in inventory, receivables and payables, loans and capital introduced.

front: Ways to improve liquidity and working capital
back: More capital or long-term loans, less inventory, faster collection from customers, longer credit from suppliers, sell unused assets, cut drawings.
Raise prices, buy more cheaply, sell higher-margin lines, reduce losses of inventory, control expenses.
This year's gross profit is overstated; next year's is understated (opening inventory too high).

front: Current ratio steady, acid test falling
back: Inventory has become a bigger share of current assets.
